newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- JOBLESS DOWN, EARNINGS UP

Official figures released yesterday showed a sharp fall in unemployment and a pick-up in average earnings. Figures for those out of work and eligible for benefit in March dropped 41,000 to 1,707,000, or 6.1 percent of the workforce. Figures also showed earnings had risen by five percent in the year to February, up from 4.5 percent in January.
-- ALLIANCE HOLDERS SELL IN ADVANCE

About 600,000 Alliance & Leicester members are selling their bonus shares in advance of the flotation planned for next Monday, about 27 percent of the qualifying customers. Institutions are being asked if they want to bid for these shares. The first auction will take place tomorrow.
-- MORE HOUSEHOLDS FREE OF NEGATIVE EQUITY TRAP

The Woolwich Building Society said negative equity had fallen to its lowest level for seven years, with two percent of homeowners now in the trap. There are now 360,000 households with negative equity, down from the 1.7 million peak in early 1993 and down 45,000 from the first quarter of this year, after the 1.3 percent rise in house prices.
THE TIMES
-- INSURANCE INDUSTRY AGGRIEVED BY BILL TO BAIL OUT IFAs

Life insurers face a bill of up to 16 million stg for the bailing-out of independent financial advisers who sold customers the wrong pensions and then collapsed. The charge has been imposed as part of a levy announced by the Investors Compensation Scheme. The Association of British Insurers protested, saying it had the costs imposed on its own members to meet and that negligent independent advisers were not their responsibility.
-- BATES WORLDWIDE BUYOUT TALKS WITH CORDIANT

The management of Bates Worldwide, the second advertising agency owned by Cordiant, is thought to be negotiating a partial buyout of the network after Cordiant rejected a proposal to sell Bates. Cordiant said it did not intend to sell the network, despite an approach from True North of the USA.
THE GUARDIAN
-- CIGARETTE MAKERS SET TO STUMP UP END TO TOBACCO WARS

The prospect of a deal to end the tobacco wars moved closer yesterday as it emerged top executives have started secret negotiations that could lead to an agreement costing the industry $300 billion over 25 years. The talks put industry figures against state attorney generals, who are suing them over the cost of treating smoking-related diseases.
-- EC PROPOSAL COSTLY FOR COMMODITY FIRMS

Commodities dealers face having to make provisions against potential market losses under legislation proposed by the European Commission. The proposals would put the 1995 Basle Agreement on Banking Supervision into EU law, allowing banks to use internal models to calculate the capital needed for protection against market risks. Such risk calculations are far more difficult and expensive for commodities dealers.
-- MARCH DEBT FALLS TO 8.8 BILLION STG

Figures released yesterday showed that government debt fell last month, mainly due to tight Treasury control of Whitehall end-of-year spending, as well as proceeds contributed from the sale of the Housing Corporation loan book. The gap between Treasury spending and receipts was 8.8 billion stg for March, against 9.5 billion stg last year.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- REGAN DEBATES WHETHER TO OPEN HOSTILITIES

Andrew Regan's Lancia Trust was yesterday meeting with advisers to try to decide whether to launch a full-scale bid for parts of the Co-operative Wholesale Society. Any bid would need to be launched before the general election, as Labour, if elected, is likely to take a tough line against it. Co-op sponsors 16 Labour MPs.
-- OFTEL MOVES HERALD MOBILE SHAKE-OUT

Telephones regulator Don Cruickshank yesterday made moves to relax restrictions on mobile phone operators. The move could speed up price restrictions for consumers. Companies will have more flexibility over how they sell, which could see a reduction in selling via service providers.
